clue.text: Seeking truth following commission of crime

parts.note: to be after something is to be seeking it
the fact is the plain truth of a matter

explanation.surface: A detective hunts for the truth once a crime has been committed.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is familiar from law, where an accessory after the crime helps the offender once the deed is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done once an offence has already happened comes later than that event, the sense of an accessory's role in law.

clue.text: One of many deliveries given as theologian

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'One of many deliveries given as theologian (7)' is held with answer ALUMNUS, copied from 8-across; the clue gives AQUINAS (A QUIN + AS), which crosses 8-across's U, but the answer cannot be corrected as it is not marked (MODEL).
annotationWithheld.clue: One of many deliveries given as theologian

clue.text: Climbing aid — catch up on proper procedure, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the letters built are swapped for a word pronounced the same

parts.note: catch is NET, written upwards as TEN in this down clue, put on DRILL, proper procedure

explanation.surface: Someone learns the correct method by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET (catch) into TEN, set on DRILL; 'we hear' gives a word that sounds like TEN DRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's slender coiling shoot wraps round supports to help it climb.

clue.text: Dire scene — ruined home

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful sight: a wrecked house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges DIRE and SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is the house or place where one lives.

clue.text: Dress sailor in clobber

indicators.note: in puts the sailor inside the other word

parts.note: to clobber is to hit hard
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman is dressed in clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clobber' is British slang for clothes, which suits the surface, but here it is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's or nun's long robe is a form of clothing.

clue.text: Avoid bygone ceremonial that's over our heads

parts.note: to fly is to flee or avoid
past means bygone

explanation.surface: Someone shuns old-fashioned pomp that goes beyond their understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over our heads' suggests something too hard to grasp, but it is literal: aircraft overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial display of aircraft passing in formation above a crowd.

clue.text: Somewhat insignificant, a tambourine in choral work

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tambourine plays a minor part in a piece for singers.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-length vocal composition with chorus and soloists, often sacred.

clue.text: Petty bureaucrat to give up post

parts.note: to jack in is British slang for giving up
a post is a job or office

explanation.surface: A small-minded official is told to resign.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-important minor official who throws his weight about.

clue.text: Former student taking mineral to North America

parts.note: alum is a mineral salt used in dyeing and tanning
US stands for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A graduate takes a rock sample across to the New World.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduate or former pupil of a school or college is called by this Latin word.

clue.text: Stab with blade — atone by reforming

indicators.note: reforming means the letters of the two words are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A violent attacker is urged to make amends by changing their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforming' rearranges ATONE and BY together.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce someone with the blade fixed to a rifle's muzzle is to use that weapon as a verb.

clue.text: Meet high art collection heading East, here?

indicators.note: heading here means travelling towards, so the compass point comes last
collection means the letters are gathered up and assembled afresh

explanation.surface: Visitors meet at a fine collection of art in a Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection' is the anagram signal and 'heading' adds the compass point at the end; 'here?' asks for the place the surface describes, the great museum in St Petersburg.
explanation.definitionFit: The great St Petersburg museum is where such an eastern art collection is housed.

clue.text: Relatives sounding frightful — they're still family

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

indicators.note: sounding says the next piece is replaced by a word it is pronounced like

parts.note: dread as an adjective means frightful, causing fear

explanation.surface: Relatives may seem dreadful, but they are still your family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns DREAD into its sound-alike DRED.
explanation.definitionFit: People related by blood remain one's family group, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Each cut in filming, get a bun

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the other piece

parts.note: a take is one spell of filming a scene

indicators.note: cut means the word Each loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Every scene trimmed during a film shoot earns the crew a sweet roll.
explanation.walkthrough: A take is one continuous filmed shot, which is why filming can stand for it; 'cut' trims the end of Each and 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, flat, sweet yeast roll with currants, usually toasted and buttered, is a kind of bun.

clue.text: Not applicable to girl sounding nosy

parts.note: NA is the usual abbreviation for not applicable on forms
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: A form notes that a question does not apply to a girl who sounds like a busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nosy' here means of the nose, not prying: a voice that comes through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A voice that resonates through the nose is described with this adjective.

clue.text: The margin in error? It's terrifying

indicators.note: in error says the letters of the words are set down wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A mistake in the margin of a page is a frightening thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges THE MARGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad dream, or any experience that frightens, is this noun.

clue.text: State detective's imprudent to enter without warrant

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state
tec is short for detective
rash means imprudent

explanation.surface: A careless police officer breaks into a property without legal authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warrant' suggests a search warrant, but here it means invitation: to turn up at a party unasked.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to a party or event uninvited is to crash the gate.

clue.text: Heavens above! Resolute soldiers in retreating army

parts.note: a firm person is resolute

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the turned-round army
retreating means the army's letters go backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve
men are soldiers in the ranks

explanation.surface: An exclamation greets resolute troops as their army pulls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the army round to AT, and 'in' sets the soldiers within it; 'Heavens above!' poses as an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The sky seen as an arch overhead is a poetic word for the heavens.

clue.text: Reading article that's been edited .

indicators.note: that's been edited says the word has been rewritten into another order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is read out after revisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been edited' rearranges ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A public performance of poetry or music, or a reciting of a text, is this noun.

clue.text: A fruit and nut not acceptable as food

parts.note: a lime is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: not acceptable means the letter for acceptable is dropped

parts.note: nut is used as written before the deletion

explanation.surface: An apple and a nut are not a suitable meal.
explanation.walkthrough: U means upper-class, so acceptable in polite society; 'not acceptable' takes U from NUT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment or sustenance is an old word for what we eat.

clue.text: Tea room's empty entrance

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: empty means the word room's is cleared of its middle, keeping only its outside letters, R and M

explanation.surface: The way into a tea room has nobody in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' takes the outside letters R and M of room, the 's adding nothing. 'entrance' is the verb, to enchant, not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to delight or enchant them, the verb sense of enrapture.

clue.text: Preserve strict honesty

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
dour means stern, strict

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to keep to rigorous truthfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankness, saying openly what one thinks, is a synonym.

clue.text: Poison — a warning signal's given about it

indicators.note: about means the cone goes around the next word

parts.note: a traffic cone warns drivers of a hazard

explanation.surface: A warning is issued about a toxic substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; a traffic cone is the warning signal placed on roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood, a plant whose root yields a deadly toxin.

clue.text: One fact about Conservative is irritating

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means the fact's word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a thing can mean a fact, as in the main thing

explanation.surface: Something about a Tory politician gets under the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts THING around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that tickles and makes one want to scratch is this adjective, hence annoying.

clue.text: Birds to observe in, say, soaring

indicators.note: soaring means rising, so in this down clue the letters read upwards
in puts the observing word inside the other

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
to see is to observe

explanation.surface: Bird-watchers are told to look at birds flying high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' builds ESEEG, and 'soaring' reads it upwards as befits a down clue; 'say' is the usual crossword signal for eg.
explanation.definitionFit: Large waterfowl, the plural of a common farmyard bird.

clue.text: Associate with criminal character

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a sort is a kind of person, as in a good sort

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep company with a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep company or mix with people, often bad ones, is to consort.

clue.text: Succeeding without new engineers, in the end

indicators.note: without means the word for new is taken away

parts.note: next means succeeding, coming after
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Someone finally succeeds even after the new engineers have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes N from NEXT, leaving EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthest point, at the outermost limit or end, is called the extreme.

clue.text: Passionate, takes trouble with token of love

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
a ring is given as a token of love

explanation.surface: An ardent suitor goes to great pains over an engagement present.
explanation.definitionFit: Loving someone deeply is to be fervent in affection.

clue.text: Drier dandy

definitions.meaning: a frame on which laundry is hung to dry
a man very concerned with his dress, a fop

explanation.definitionFit: The wooden airer for washing and the fop who shows off clothes share the name.
